title: Automate zero-downtime data-plane rollouts and deterministic rollback for Private/VPC runtime upgrades
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Goal: implement an automated, auditable workflow to perform data-plane/runtime upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments with strong guarantees: zero-downtime during normal upgrades, deterministic automated rollback on safety signals, and easy on-call remediation. This work covers orchestration glue (Terraform/IaC changes, orchestration playbooks), runtime drain/bringup logic, health-check criteria, canary/ phased rollout strategies, and the rollback/circuit-breaker mechanisms.

Scope: nodes in customer-managed VPCs (VM or k8s), Redwood Private runtime (inference serving processes, KV cache, local cache drains), autoscaler and LB interactions, and integration points with Console for rollout observability and manual aborts. Not in scope: control-plane schema migrations or changes that require customer migration windows (those will be separate coordinated upgrades).
acceptance_criteria: Automated rollout can upgrade a typical 10-node customer deployment with <1% error budget consumption and no dropped requests (observed in integration test harness)
Canary stage detects regressions based on latency p95, error-rate, and model output hash checks and aborts with automated rollback within configured thresholds
Rollback path returns cluster to pre-upgrade binary/artifact and restores in-flight KV/connection state where possible, and produces a post-mortem artifact with timeline and metrics
Terraform modules and runbooks updated so SRE/SEs can trigger upgrades via the Console or CLI with audit logs retained
design_notes: Adopt a three-stage rollout: canary (1 node), staggered (% of capacity at 10/30/60/100), final sweep. Each stage gated by health checks and regression detectors.

Health checks: (1) probe /ready endpoint post-start, (2) end-to-end synthetic inference call measuring p50/p95 and correctness hash, (3) KV cache warm-up success (local metrics), (4) connection draining complete for node before termination.

Drain strategy: use graceful SIGTERM + wait-for-kv-flush script that flushes/streams KV deltas to shared store, keep accepting requests during short handoff via connection proxy until in-flight requests complete, then remove from LB target group.

Rollback: maintain immutable artifacts and keep previous artifact available in the cluster. On fail, deploy previous artifact to newly-created nodes first, wait for health gates, then progressively return traffic. Avoid stateful DB schema changes in same workflow.

Terraform/IaC: add an "upgrade_plan" module that sequences instance group replacements with pre/post hooks (Lambda or remote-exec) and exposes variables to configure canary size, health thresholds, and timeout windows.

Observability: emit rollout events to Console (per-stage metrics), OpenTelemetry traces for the upgrade actions, and a synthetic-run dashboard that compares pre/post distributions. Capture per-node logs to a temporary S3/GCS bundle for quick triage.

Safety: circuit breaker that can auto-abort when error rates exceed configured thresholds OR when critical customers with pinned versions are impacted. Manual abort must be one CLI call with immediate stop and rollback initiation.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 - PoC: implement canary flow in staging using existing k8s deployments. Build test harness to simulate 500rps traffic with representative prompts. (owner: Ravi)

Phase 1 - IaC: add upgrade_plan module to terraform-private-modules, include pre-hook for KV drain, post-hook for healthcheck verification, and variables for stage sizes. Add unit tests for module using terratest. (owner: Infra team)

Phase 2 - Orchestration: implement orchestration lambda/service that sequences canary -> ramp -> sweep using Terraform or k8s rolling replacement primitives. Integrate with Console to show progress. (owner: Orchestration)
Phase 3 - Rollback: implement deterministic rollback logic and rollback-runbook generator. Include time-travel artifact records so we can redeploy previous SHA. (owner: Ravi)
Phase 4 - Hardening: run upgrade rehearsals against Canary customers and internal infra, capture metrics and tune health thresholds. (owner: SRE + SE)
Phase 5 - Launch: enable feature flag to allow scheduled upgrades for opt-in customers, document runbook and run a company-wide training session. (owner: Product Ops)
Estimated total: 8 points; parallel work across infra and orchestration recommended.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV cache inconsistency after rolling older artifact back -> Mitigation: ensure KV flush-to-shared-store and replay mechanism; block upgrades that include KV schema changes.

Risk: Lambda/orchestration outage during rollout leading to partial upgrades -> Mitigation: orchestration is idempotent; store progress state in durable store (Dynamo/postgres) and allow manual resume/rollback.

Risk: Customer firewalls / network ACLs prevent health probes -> Mitigation: support out-of-band health reporting agent that can reach Console via customer's egress or use an agentless SSH-based probe with customer permission.
Risk: Terraform drift or conflicting manual changes -> Mitigation: run plan + dry-run gate; fail upgrade if applied state drift detected; add pre-check to verify IaC drift < threshold.
Risk: Long-lived connections (gRPC streams) -> Mitigation: support graceful drain with connection handoff and short-circuit new connections to canaries when necessary.
Risk: Secret/KMS rotation required mid-upgrade -> Mitigation: block upgrade if KMS key versions differ; add preflight KMS check and include secret-rotation window in upgrade plan.
test_plan: Unit tests for terraform module (terratest) and unit tests for orchestration state machine
End-to-end integration test in staging with synthetic traffic, verifying zero 5xx spikes and <5% p95 regression during ramp
Chaos test: randomly kill nodes during upgrade to validate rollback and resume behavior
Customer-like test: run on a staging VPC that mirrors customer network topologies (NAT, private subnets) to validate healthcheck reachability
Canary regression criteria: p95 latency increase >15% OR error-rate increase >0.5% OR correctness hash mismatch -> abort and rollback
runbook_snippets: CLI to start upgrade: rwctl upgrades start --cluster-id CL-abc123 --artifact sha:2025abcd --canary-size 1 --stages 10,30,60,100
Abort/rollback: rwctl upgrades abort --upgrade-id UPG-20250304 --reason "canary regression" (triggers automatic rollback to previous artifact)
Get status: rwctl upgrades status --upgrade-id UPG-20250304 --output json

If rollback fails: contact on-call SRE (pager) and run rwctl upgrades force-rollback --upgrade-id UPG-20250304 to spin new nodes with previous artifact and reattach storage; collect logs from /var/log/redwood/upgrade-*.tgz
